arxiv-1912-08930.title: Graphlets in Multiplex Networks
arxiv-1912-08930.creator: Tamara Dimitrova, Kristijan Petrovski, Ljupco Kocarev
arxiv-1912-08930.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Tamara Dimitrova, Kristijan Petrovski, Ljupco Kocarev. We develop graphlet analysis for multiplex networks and discuss how this analysis can be extended to multilayer and multilevel networks as well as to graphs with node and/or link categorical attributes. The analysis has been adapted for two typical examples of multiplexes: economic trade data represented as a 957-plex network and 75 social networks each represented as a 12-plex network.

arxiv-2105-07538.description: Abstract There is increasing interest in detecting collective anomalies: potentially short periods of time where the features of data change before reverting back to normal behaviour. arxiv-2109-04650.title: What Changes Can Large-scale Language Models Bring? Intensive Study on HyperCLOVA: Billions-scale Korean Generative Pretrained Transformers
arxiv-2109-04650.creator: Boseop Kim HyoungSeok Kim Sang-Woo Lee Gichang Lee, Donghyun Kwak Dong Hyeon Jeon Sunghyun Park Sungju Kim, Seonhoon Kim Dongpil Seo Heungsub Lee Minyoung Jeong Sungjae Lee, Minsub Kim Suk Hyun Ko Seokhun Kim Taeyong Park Jinuk Kim, Soyoung Kang Na-Hyeon Ryu Kang Min Yoo Minsuk Chang Soobin Suh, Soo
arxiv-2109-04650.description: Abstract GPT-3 shows remarkable in-context learning ability of large-scale language models (LMs) trained on hundreds of billion scale data. Here we address some remaining issues less reported by the GPT-3 paper, such as a non-English LM, the performances of different sized models, and the effect of recently introduced prompt optimization on in-context learning.

arxiv-2304-07102.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by You-An Lee, Sander G. Huisman, Detlef Lohse. We inject with jet mixtures of ethanol and dissolved anise oil upward into quiescent water with jet Reynolds numbers, 500 < R ​ e 0 < 810 500<Re_{0}<810 . arxiv-2307-09356.title: OnlineRefer: A Simple Online Baseline for Referring Video Object Segmentation
arxiv-2307-09356.creator: Dongming Wu, Tiancai Wang, Yuang Zhang, Xiangyu Zhang, Jianbing Shen
arxiv-2307-09356.description: Abstract Referring video object segmentation (RVOS) aims at segmenting an object in a video following human instruction. Current state-of-the-art methods fall into an offline pattern, in which each clip independently interacts with text embedding for cross-modal understanding. They usually present that the offline pattern is necessary for RVOS, yet model limited temporal association within each clip.

arxiv-2402-04072.title: Coupling between magnetic and thermodynamic properties in R R Rh 2 Si 2 ( R R = Dy, Ho)
arxiv-2402-04072.creator: H. Dawczak-Dębicki, K. Kliemt, M. V. Ale Crivillero, R. Küchler, C. Krellner, O. Stockert, S. Wirth
arxiv-2402-04072.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by H. Dawczak-Dębicki, K. Kliemt, M. V. Ale Crivillero, R. Küchler, C. Krellner, O. Stockert, S. Wirth. Single crystals of DyRh 2 Si 2 and HoRh 2 Si 2 were investigated by thermal expansion and magnetostriction. The different types of magnetic order can clearly be seen in these measurements, particularly the canting of the moments away from the crystallographic c c direction below about 12 K and the spin-flip for magnetic field applied along the c c direction.

Successive Interference Cancellation is becoming a key building block of multiple access channel receiver, in an effort to support massive Internet of Things.

arxiv-2407-08688.title: A Unifying Categorical View of Nondeterministic Iteration and Tests
arxiv-2407-08688.creator: Sergey Goncharov, Tarmo Uustalu
arxiv-2407-08688.description: Abstract We study Kleene iteration in the categorical context. A celebrated completeness result by Kozen introduced Kleene algebra (with tests) as a ubiquitous tool for lightweight reasoning about program equivalence, and yet, numerous variants of it came along afterwards to answer the demand for more refined flavors of semantics, such as stateful, concurrent, exceptional, hybrid, branching time, etc.

arxiv-2503-16220.title: A Mean Field Game System and a Related Deterministic Optimal Control Problem
arxiv-2503-16220.creator: Ştefana-Lucia Aniţa
arxiv-2503-16220.description: Abstract This paper concerns a Mean Field Game (MFG) system related to a Nash type equilibrium for dynamical games associated to large populations. One shows that the MFG system may be viewed as the Euler-Lagrange system for an optimal control problem related to a Fokker-Planck equation with control in the drift.

arxiv-2503-22906.title: SocialGen: Modeling Multi-Human Social Interaction with Language Models
arxiv-2503-22906.creator: Heng Yu *, Juze Zhang *, Changan Chen, Tiange Xiang, Yusu Fang, Ehsan Adeli
arxiv-2503-22906.description: Abstract Human interactions in everyday life are inherently social, involving engagements with diverse individuals across various contexts. Modeling these social interactions is fundamental to a wide range of real-world applications. In this paper, we introduce SocialGen, the first unified motion-language model capable of modeling interaction behaviors among varying numbers of individuals, to address this crucial yet challenging problem.

pmc-10671890.title: Intravenous Diuresis in Severe Precapillary Pulmonary-Hypertension-Related Right Heart Failure: Effects on Renal Function and Blood Pressure
pmc-10671890.creator: Lyana Labrada, Carlos Romero, Ahmed Sadek, Danielle Belardo, Yasmin Raza, Paul Forfia, Michele Correale, Silvano Dragonieri
pmc-10671890.description: In patients with right heart failure (RHF) and pulmonary hypertension (PH), classical teaching often advises cautious diuresis in the setting of ‘preload dependence’ to avoid renal injury and hemodynamic compromise. However, while this physiology may hold true in some clinical settings, such as acute ischemia with right ventricular infarction, it cannot necessarily be extended to PH-related RHF.

pmc-11399407.title: Conserved transcriptional regulation by BRN1 and BRN2 in neocortical progenitors drives mammalian neural specification and neocortical expansion
pmc-11399407.creator: Soraia Barão, Yijun Xu, José P Llongueras, Rachel Vistein, Loyal Goff, Kristina J Nielsen, Byoung-Il Bae, Richard S Smith, Christopher A Walsh, Genevieve Stein-O’Brien, Ulrich Müller
pmc-11399407.description: The neocortex varies in size and complexity among mammals due to the tremendous variability in the number and diversity of neuronal subtypes across species. The increased cellular diversity is paralleled by the expansion of the pool of neocortical progenitors and the emergence of indirect neurogenesis during brain evolution.

pmc-11477110.title: The Definition, Diagnosis, and Management of Giant Splenic Artery Aneurysms and Pseudoaneurysms: A Systematic Review
pmc-11477110.creator: Valerio Rinaldi, Giulio Illuminati, Roberto Caronna, Giampaolo Prezioso, Piergaspare Palumbo, Paolina Saullo, Vito D’Andrea, Priscilla Nardi
pmc-11477110.description: Background/Objectives: Giant splenic artery aneurysms (SAAs) and pseudoaneurysms (SAPs) represent rare conditions, characterized by a diameter greater than or equal to 5 cm. The risk of rupture is increased compared to common SAAs and SAPs, necessitating urgent treatments to prevent it. Methods: This systematic review was conducted through a comprehensive search involving the PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus databases.

pmc-11640460.title: Synergistic Strategies for KMT2A-Rearranged Leukemias: Beyond Menin Inhibitor
pmc-11640460.creator: Sandra Cantilena, Mohamed AlAmeri, Noelia Che, Owen Williams, Jasper de Boer, Margaret T Kasner
pmc-11640460.description: Simple SummaryKMT2A-rearranged leukemias are an aggressive form of leukemia with high relapse rates, even after intensive treatment. While menin inhibitors have shown promise in early clinical trials, many patients eventually relapse due to resistance. Here, we explore alternative strategies to be used in combination with menin inhibitors to improve patient outcomes.

pmc-11816087.title: Economic impact of COVID-19 on patients with type 2 diabetes in Kenya and Tanzania: a costing analysis
pmc-11816087.creator: Caroline H Karugu, Peter Binyaruka, Patrick G Ilboudo, Richard E Sanya, Shukri F Mohamed, Lyagamula Kisia, Peter Kibe, Irene Mashiashi, Christopher Bunn, F Mair, Charles Agyemang, Sally M Mtenga, Gershim Asiki, Cindy M Gray, Eleanor Grieve, Manuela Deidda
pmc-11816087.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionCOVID-19 affected healthcare access, utilisation and affordability, especially for patients suffering from chronic diseases, including type 2 diabetes (T2D). This study measured the occurrence and magnitude of changes in healthcare and broader societal costs among patients with T2D before and during COVID-19 in Kenya and Tanzania to understand whether and how COVID-19 affected T2D management in countries implementing different policies during the pandemic.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted in Kenya and Tanzania in March–April 2022 among 500 patients with T2D in each country.

pmc-13213048.title: Individual differences reveal distinct age-related reorganizations in spatial channels for luminance and texture processing
pmc-13213048.creator: Seung Hyun Min, Alexandre Reynaud
pmc-13213048.description: Aging impairs vision, but its specific impact on the neural channels underlying pattern processing is unknown. By examining individual differences in behavioral data from 52 younger and 50 older adults, we investigated how aging reorganizes underlying channels for detecting first-order (defined by luminance static or in motion) and second-order (defined by contrast, motion, or orientation) patterns.
